::: {#exm-normal-normal}
#### Posterior for a Gaussian mean

Suppose that, given the mean $\mean$,
$\dsn{X} \siid \ndist{\mean, 1}$,
so the variance is known,
and that the prior for $\mean$ is $\ndist{0, 1}$.
Let $\vx = (\dsn{x})$ be the observed data,
with sample mean $\bar x$.

The likelihood is

$$
\ba
\p(\vx \mid \mean)
&= \prodin (2\pi)^{-1/2} \expf{-\frac{1}{2}(x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(independent Gaussian observations)}\\
&= (2\pi)^{-n/2} \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\sumin (x_i - \mean)^2}
&& \text{(combining the exponents)}\\
&= (2\pi)^{-n/2} \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\sumin \paren{x_i^2 - 2 \mean x_i + \mean^2}}
&& \text{(expanding each square)}\\
&= (2\pi)^{-n/2} \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{\sumin x_i^2 - \sumin 2 \mean x_i + \sumin \mean^2}}
&& \text{(splitting the sum)}\\
&= (2\pi)^{-n/2} \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{\sumin x_i^2 - 2 \mean \sumin x_i + \sumin \mean^2}}
&& \text{(factoring the constant $2 \mean$ out of the middle sum)}\\
&= (2\pi)^{-n/2} \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{\sumin x_i^2 - 2 \mean \sumin x_i + n \mean^2}}
&& \text{(summing the constant $\mean^2$ over $n$ terms)}\\
&= (2\pi)^{-n/2} \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{\sumin x_i^2 - 2 \mean n \bar x + n \mean^2}}
&& \text{(substituting $\sumin x_i = n \bar x$)}\\
&= (2\pi)^{-n/2} \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{\sumin x_i^2 + \paren{n \mean^2 - 2 \mean n \bar x}}}
&& \text{(reordering and grouping the terms that involve $\mean$)}\\
&= (2\pi)^{-n/2} \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\sumin x_i^2 - \frac{1}{2}\paren{n \mean^2 - 2 \mean n \bar x}}
&& \text{(distributing $-\tfrac{1}{2}$)}\\
&= (2\pi)^{-n/2} \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\sumin x_i^2}
  \cdot \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{n \mean^2 - 2 \mean n \bar x}}
&& \text{(writing the exponential of a sum as a product of exponentials)}\\
&\propto \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{n \mean^2 - 2 \mean n \bar x}}
&& \text{(dropping factors that do not involve $\mean$)},
\ea
$$ {#eq-normal-normal-exm}

and the prior density is $\p(\mean) \propto \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\mean^2}$.
Let $m \eqdef \frac{n}{n+1} \bar x$.
By @cor-bayes-proportional,

$$
\ba
\p(\mean \mid \vx)
&\propto \p(\vx \mid \mean)\, \p(\mean)
&& \text{(posterior is proportional to likelihood times prior)}\\
&\propto \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{n \mean^2 - 2 \mean n \bar x}}
  \cdot \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\mean^2}
&& \text{(substituting likelihood and prior)}\\
&= \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{n \mean^2 - 2 \mean n \bar x} - \frac{1}{2}\mean^2}
&& \text{(writing a product of exponentials as the exponential of a sum)}\\
&= \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{n \mean^2 - 2 \mean n \bar x + \mean^2}}
&& \text{(factoring out $-\tfrac{1}{2}$)}\\
&= \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{n \mean^2 + \mean^2 - 2 \mean n \bar x}}
&& \text{(reordering the terms)}\\
&= \expf{-\frac{1}{2}\paren{(n+1)\mean^2 - 2 \mean n \bar x}}
&& \text{(collecting the $\mean^2$ terms)}\\
&= \expf{-\frac{1}{2}(n+1)\paren{\mean^2 - 2 \mean \frac{n}{n+1} \bar x}}
&& \text{(factoring out $n+1$)}\\
&= \expf{-\frac{1}{2}(n+1)\paren{\mean^2 - 2 \mean m}}
&& \text{(definition of $m$)}\\
&= \expf{-\frac{1}{2}(n+1)\paren{(\mean - m)^2 - m^2}}
&& \text{(completing the square)}\\
&\propto \expf{-\frac{1}{2}(n+1)(\mean - m)^2}
&& \text{(dropping the factor $\expf{\tfrac{1}{2}(n+1)m^2}$)}.
\ea
$$ {#eq-normal-normal-exm-2}

The last line is,
up to a constant,
the density of a Gaussian distribution with mean $m$ and variance $1/(n+1)$,
so the posterior is

$$
\mean \mid \vx \;\sim\; \ndist{\frac{n}{n+1}\bar{x},\; \frac{1}{n+1}}.
$$ {#eq-normal-normal-exm-3}

The posterior mean $\frac{n}{n+1}\bar{x}$ is the sample mean
shrunk toward the prior mean $0$,
and the shrinkage factor $\frac{n}{n+1}$ approaches $1$ as $n \to \infty$.
:::
